# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.9 on Thu Aug 06 11:00:00 2026
# A small VPS that became someone else's weapon. Nothing here is "hacked":
# every rule was added on purpose, and the box works fine. The damage lands
# on strangers, because UDP takes no handshake — these services answer a
# forged source address, so an attacker sends a small query claiming the
# victim's IP and this host mails the victim a much bigger reply.
#
# The DNS resolver started out right (port 53 for the LAN only, still here
# on the line above) — then someone "widened it while debugging" and left
# the second, source-less copy in place: an open resolver, up to 54x.
# NTP was opened because "the clock kept drifting", but with -m limit in
# front: a total ceiling is exactly the right control for amplification,
# so that one is NOT flagged — it caps what this host can emit.
# memcached got its UDP port opened so "the other container could reach
# it": 51,000x, the multiplier behind the 1.35 Tbps GitHub flood in 2018.
# And SSDP is on because a media server asked for it — 30x, and nothing
# outside the LAN ever needed to discover anything here.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 -j DROP
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 53 -s 192.168.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 123 -m limit --limit 10/sec -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 11211 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 1900 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m limit --limit 5/min -j LOG --log-prefix "[fw-input-drop] " --log-level 4
COMMIT
